title: Hierarchical workload sieve + safe-splay rollout for automated batching recommendations
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a recommendation engine that profiles workloads at multiple granularities (route, model, customer cohort, temporal windows) using a 'hierarchical workload sieve' to produce safe, incremental batching and caching parameter suggestions. Implement a rollout controller called 'safe-splay' that staggers application across micro-cohorts with randomized splay windows, shadow verification, and automatic rollback when leading indicators exceed thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Sieve profiler produces per-route and per-cohort workload signatures (p95 latency, token distribution, KV hit ratio) in production shadow mode
Recommendation output includes batching config: target_max_batch, max_wait_ms, kv_prefix_cache_policy, and confidence score
Safe-splay rollout applies recommendations to <5% micro-cohorts with randomized splay and collects shadow metrics for 24h before widening
Automatic rollback triggers if error_rate increases >30% relative or latency p95 regresses >20% for the cohort
Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-cohort cost delta estimate, applied cohort list, rollback reason, and linked PR/commit
End-to-end smoke test in staging simulates bursty traffic and validates no regressions when safe-splay applies changes

implementation_notes: Profiler will emit compact signatures: median_seq_len, seq_len_quantiles, kv_prefix_hit_estimate, arrival_rate_histogram. The recommendation model combines deterministic heuristics (safety bounds) + a small supervised regressor trained from past safe-rollouts to produce confidence. Safe-splay controller applies changes with exponential splay windows (initial cohort ~0.5-2% traffic, then 4%, then 12%) and requires stable shadow metrics for 24h between steps. Rollback uses a three-strike rule: (1) immediate safety signal: spike in 5xxs, (2) short-term signal: >20% p95 regression for 30m, (3) cost signal: negative business metric (tokens-per-invocation drop) for 6h.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive batching could cause tokenization/sequence-length corner cases that blow KV cache. Mitigation: add a conservative kv_prefix_cache_policy that disables prefix caching for cohorts with >10% outlier long sequences and ensure canary cohorts include synthetic long-sequence probes. Risk: telemetry blind spots during rollout. Mitigation: require minimum telemetry coverage (>=1000 requests/day) before any cohort receives changes.
manual_steps_for_emergency_rollback: 1) Use Console 'Safe-Splay' -> Active Cohorts -> Force Rollback on cohort ID. 2) If console unavailable, run rtictl rollback --cohort <id> --reason "auto-rollback" which toggles per-route batch params back to previous commit and triggers an immediate soft-evict of new KV entries. 3) Open incident channel #runtime-rollback and notify SRE on-call.
related_work_notes: This ticket complements ENG-7421 (autotune-batching-profiles) but focuses on multi-granularity profiling and rollout safety. It will feed recommendations into the batching-autotune pipeline and uses telemetry schemas extended by ENG-30911.
